metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets North Macedonia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for North Macedonia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD reporting is based on the PISA technical standards and associated sampling/estimation procedures. The factsheet itself does not specify the exact student weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used, so analysts should follow the PISA 2022 technical documentation and the OECD Reader’s Guide for the correct weight and variance-estimation approach. Plausible values are used for cognitive achievement reporting in PISA; however, this factsheet presents summary statistics and does not document the PV-combining method or missing-data handling at the factsheet level.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than an empirical analysis paper that specifies how plausible values and missing data were handled in a re-analysis. The factsheet reports OECD-produced estimates (means, proficiency shares, and correlations) without documenting the PV-combining rule or the missing-data procedure used in the underlying OECD database production. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported at the level required for extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the North Macedonia PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment sample: 6,610 students in 111 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science and for whom creative thinking results are reported in this factsheet. The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the OECD PISA implementation and technical standards; it reports the analytic sample used for the North Macedonia estimates.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-olds in North Macedonia, based on the PISA 2022 creative thinking cognitive test implemented in 64 countries and economies (with North Macedonia included). The creative thinking test comprises 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). North Macedonia’s mean creative thinking score is 19 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency shares (34% at Level 3+ vs 78% OECD average; 8% at Level 5/6 vs 27% OECD average) and relative strengths/weaknesses across ideation processes and domain contexts. It further documents within-country gaps by socioeconomic status and gender, and associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance, while noting COVID-19-related implementation cautions for some countries/economies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It does not train or evaluate machine learning models, and it does not provide the methodological details (e.g., PV-combining rule, missing-data procedure, or model performance metrics) required to populate ML-specific fields. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally left empty because the document reports descriptive and OECD-estimated outcomes rather than a re-analysis with specified predictors and predictive targets.
